history.period: Chola period, 11th century; Vijayanagara expansion 14th-15th century
history.summary: The grand Someshwara Temple in Kolar's Fort Area, a five-minute walk from the Kolaramma Temple, was built by the Cholas in the 11th century and later expanded by the Vijayanagara Empire; Kolar district sources describe it as an example of 14th-century Vijayanagara art. It is a fine Dravidian complex with a rajagopuram, pillared mandapas and a celebrated Kalyana Mantapa whose carved pillars include motifs with international/trade connections; a large temple tank stands outside. The main sanctum houses the Shiva lingam of Lord Someshwara. The temple shares a priest with the Kolaramma Temple. One travel review claims ASI protection - UNVERIFIED (verify).

name: Someshwara Temple
town_description: Kolar, about 70 km east of Bengaluru, is one of Karnataka's oldest cities - known in antiquity as Kolahala, Kuvalala and Kolala, and once the capital of the Western Gangas. Nicknamed the 'Golden Land of India' for the historic Kolar Gold Fields nearby, it is a temple town whose landmarks include the Kolaramma and Someshwara temples, Antaragange hill, and the Avani temple cluster.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 80 km (verify).
travel.road: In the Fort Area of Kolar town on NH-75 (Bengaluru-Kolar-Mulbagal road); about 70-80 km from Bengaluru (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri is the grandest festival.
